scope.description: Three-voter in-process cluster {A,B,C} at protocol version 3 with 50ms timeouts. A snapshots, then C is shut down for its own removal, RemoveServer C commits with {A,B}, two further commands push the persisted commit index past the removal entry, and A is restarted on the same stores with RestoreCommittedLogs (case restore_on) or without it (control restore_off). The restarted A's configuration and peer count are observed against B's. Then C is brought back on its old stores so it catches up from A, B is partitioned from A, and one Apply is issued on A; the probe records whether the Apply succeeded, the entry index, A's commit and applied indexes, whether the entry reached B, and the FSM lengths on both sides.
assumptions: C is offline for its own removal, so it never learns it was removed; that is an ordinary operator sequence (a failed node is removed while down and then comes back).
B and C both hold every entry up to the removal, so the entries, commit index and configurations come from real replication.
After the partition, {A,B} is the configuration committed in the log (removal entry committed), so an entry present only on A cannot be committed.
excluded: No disk faults or message loss; the only partition is the explicit disconnection of B.
The probe does not assert what happens after the partition heals, which is the subject of the dual-majority harness.

basis.prefix: Real bootstrap of all three voters, real snapshot, real RemoveServer, real commits, real shutdown/restart of the leader and of the removed voter on the same InmemCommitTrackingStore/InmemStore/InmemSnapshotStore instances, real transport reconnection and real partition. No fabricated configuration or log state.

comparisons.description: A restarted leader must not count a voter whose removal is committed in its own log.
Control: the same restart without RestoreCommittedLogs keeps the committed membership.
An entry whose Apply reported success on the stale-membership leader must be present on a quorum of the configuration committed in the log ({A,B} requires both members).
Control: with the committed membership the same partition must make the leader refuse the write.

revision_reason: The executed run confirmed the membership resurrection but never reached the write prediction: the retained log shows B winning the election in term 3 right after A's restart, so A was a follower when the write was issued and the Apply returned a leadership error. Two harness faults are corrected: B's heartbeat/election timeouts are reloaded to 3s before A restarts so the stale leader wins its re-election, and the harness now records whether A is leader before the partition and takes the compared index from the Apply future itself, emitting the quorum field only when the write was acknowledged. C's own restart is also kept on the normal path (flag disabled) so a configuration-less C cannot confound the election.
